name: nav-build
description: Navigate to the Build / pipeline screen and park the UI in its resting state. Recorded against the design demo, but written to be portable: it drives the UI the way a user would (click the Build tab) rather than relying on the demo's default page prop, so the identical script can be replayed against web/app.
notes: The demo's locked variant defaults already land on Build with pipelineStyle='Flow chart (6d)'; the explicit tab click is a no-op there and a real navigation in the rewrite.
Selectors are the demo's own: .tb-tab for the top-level tabs, [data-pg]/[data-on] for page visibility. web/app must expose equivalent hooks or this script needs a per-target selector map.

Portrait viewports (1024x1366, 900w, 768w) are covered by the demo's designed 'Rotate to landscape' gate (.rot). Steps that touch the app chrome carry skipIfVisible: '.rot' so those viewports still produce a baseline of the gate itself instead of a click timeout.

steps.name: 00-app-mounted
steps.note: App shell has mounted and the top nav is interactive. (Do not wait on [data-pg] alone: every page host exists in the DOM from the start and the first one, Login, is hidden.)

steps.name: 02-build-page-active
steps.note: Build page host is the active one.

steps.name: 03-park-cursor
steps.note: No hover state may be baked into a baseline.

steps.name: 04-drop-focus
steps.note: No focus ring may be baked into a baseline.

steps.name: 05-settled
steps.note: Burn the fixed virtual-time budget again so streaming/animated content lands on its deterministic end state.
